settings.saved: Saved {count, plural, one {# setting} other {# settings}}
settings.dirty: {count, plural, one {# unsaved change} other {# unsaved changes}}

secret.placeholder: Leave empty to keep the current value
secret.clearHint: It goes back to the default (empty). This cannot be undone.

markdown.hint: Markdown is supported, HTML is not. At most {max, number} characters.

image.hint: Square PNG, {min}–{max} pixels on each side, up to 1 MiB. Images under 64 pixels are treated as pixel art and scaled up by a whole number.

testMail.hint: Sends a test email to your address {email} using the saved settings. Save your changes first.
testMail.sent: Test email sent to {to}. Check the inbox.

testCaptcha.hint: Solve the captcha once with the saved settings and verify it the way sign-in does, to check the site key, the secret key and the server’s network. Save your changes first.
testCaptcha.notConfigured: Choose a provider, fill in both keys and save to test the captcha here.
testCaptcha.title: Test the captcha
testCaptcha.description: Solve the captcha below, then select “Verify”.
testCaptcha.incomplete: Solve the captcha first, then select “Verify”.
testCaptcha.passedHint: The captcha is set up correctly. Sign-up, password sign-in and password reset will require it.
testCaptcha.failedHint: The provider rejected this attempt. Try again; if it keeps failing, check that this site’s domain is allowed for the site key.
testCaptcha.unavailableHint: The server couldn't complete the check: the secret key is wrong or the provider is unreachable. Until this is fixed nobody can sign in or sign up, so fix it or set the provider to “Disabled”.

provider.label: Captcha provider
provider.help: Required for every registration, password sign-in, and password reset request. Enabled only when both keys are set. reCAPTCHA uses www.recaptcha.net.

siteKey.label: Site key
siteKey.help: Public key passed to the captcha widget on the page.

secretKey.label: Secret key
secretKey.help: Used only on the server to verify captcha tokens. Never sent back to the browser.

recaptchaInvisible.label: Invisible reCAPTCHA
recaptchaInvisible.help: Applies only to reCAPTCHA and must match the key type: v2 checkbox and invisible widgets use different keys.

name.label: Site name
name.help: Shown in the header, the browser tab and emails. Launchers show it as the name of the authentication server.

logo.label: Site logo
logo.help: Replaces the block-head mark in the header, the footer and the sign-in pages; the site name stays beside it. A transparent image of 64 pixels or more works best.

favicon.label: Site icon
favicon.help: The icon in browser tabs, bookmarks and on phone home screens. Without one, the site logo is used. Use 180 pixels or more so it looks sharp on home screens; transparent parts get a white background there.

description.label: Site description
description.help: A sentence below the home page heading and footer logo, also used as the page meta description. Leave it empty to use the default introduction.

keywords.label: Page keywords
keywords.help: The page meta keywords. One per line, up to 32 entries with 1–64 characters each.

url.label: Site URL
url.help: The full address people use to reach this site, for example https://skin.example.com. Links in emails and external login use it, and in production nobody can sign in until it is set. After a domain change, existing passkeys stop working.

locale.label: Default language
locale.help: Used when someone has not chosen a language and their browser offers none that this site supports.

timeZone.label: Time zone
timeZone.help: Dates and times are shown in this time zone, and the daily check-in reset follows it. Use an IANA name such as Asia/Shanghai.

announcement.label: Announcement
announcement.help: Shown on the user dashboard. Leave it empty to hide it.

footer.label: Footer text
footer.help: One line at the bottom of the footer. Supports Markdown; {year} becomes the current year. Leave it empty to show “© year site name”. For an ICP registration link, for example: [京ICP备12345678号](https://beian.miit.gov.cn/).

enabled.label: Open registration
enabled.help: When off, new people cannot sign up. Existing users can still sign in.

withPlayerName.label: Ask for a player name at sign-up
withPlayerName.help: Creates a player during sign-up and uses its name as the nickname. When off, people enter a nickname instead.

perIpLimit.label: Accounts per IP
perIpLimit.help: How many accounts one IP address can register. 0 means no limit.

emailDomains.label: Email domains
emailDomains.help: Which email addresses can be used to sign up. Domains must match exactly; subdomains are not included.

domains.label: Domains
domains.help: One per line, for example example.com.

requireEmailVerification.label: Require a verified email
requireEmailVerification.help: When on, people who have not verified their email cannot manage players or textures, use their closet, or report textures. Set up email first.

initialScore.label: Starting score
initialScore.help: Score given to new users when they sign up.

perPlayer.label: Cost of a player
perPlayer.help: Score charged for each player someone adds.

perKbPublic.label: Storage cost of public textures
perKbPublic.help: Score charged per KB when uploading a public texture.

perKbPrivate.label: Storage cost of private textures
perKbPrivate.help: Score charged per KB when uploading a private texture. Making a public texture private charges the difference.

perClosetItem.label: Cost of a closet item
perClosetItem.help: Score charged for each texture added to a closet.

refundOnDelete.label: Refund on deletion
refundOnDelete.help: Refund what was actually paid when a player or texture is deleted.

score.label: Check-in reward
score.help: Each check-in gives a random score in this range. Use the same number twice for a fixed reward.

gapHours.label: Check-in interval
gapHours.help: Minimum number of hours between two check-ins.

resetAtMidnight.label: Reset check-in at midnight
resetAtMidnight.help: When on, people can check in again after midnight in the site time zone, regardless of the interval.

cost.label: Cost of a report
cost.help: Score charged when submitting a report. Refunded if the report is upheld, kept if it is dismissed.

reward.label: Report reward
reward.help: Extra score given to the reporter when a report is upheld.

nameRule.label: Player name rule
nameRule.help: Which characters player names may contain.

options.official: Letters, digits and underscores (like official accounts)

nameRegex.label: Custom player name rule
nameRegex.help: The regular expression used when the rule is “Custom”, in JavaScript syntax with the u flag. Leave it empty for no restriction.

uuidAlgorithm.label: UUIDs of new players
uuidAlgorithm.help: Only affects players created from now on. Existing players keep their UUIDs forever.

options.offline: Derived from the name (same as offline mode)

maxPerUser.label: Players per user
maxPerUser.help: How many players a regular user can have. 0 means no limit. Admins and super admins are not limited. Transferring a player in the admin panel also checks this limit; after lowering it, existing players are kept, but users over the limit cannot add more.

nameRegex.label: Texture name rule
nameRegex.help: A regular expression texture names must match, in JavaScript syntax with the u flag. Leave it empty for no restriction.

contentPolicy.label: Content policy
contentPolicy.help: Shown on the upload page to explain which textures are not allowed. Leave it empty to hide it.

transport.label: Delivery
transport.help: Without email, verifying addresses and resetting passwords are unavailable.

smtp.label: SMTP server
smtp.help: Leave the username empty if the server does not require login.

from.label: Sender
from.help: The address is required; no email can be sent without it.

signingKey.label: Signing key
signingKey.help: The RSA private key, at least 4096 bits, that signs players’ texture data. External login is unavailable without it. Paste a PEM key or generate one.
signingKey.generateHint: Game servers only pick up the new public key after a restart. Until then they cannot verify the new signatures, and player skins may not show. The old key is not kept, so this cannot be undone.

skinDomains.label: Allowed texture domains
skinDomains.help: Domains besides this site that textures may be loaded from. One per line; a leading dot includes subdomains, for example .example.com.

profileSearchLimit.label: Bulk player lookup limit
profileSearchLimit.help: How many players a game server can look up by name in one request.

apiLocationIndication.label: Send API location indication
apiLocationIndication.help: Adds the X-Authlib-Injector-API-Location header to responses, so entering the site’s home page in a launcher also finds the external login API.

tokenValidSeconds.label: Token validity
tokenValidSeconds.help: Seconds. Tokens can join servers, validate and change textures during this period. Applies to launcher logins and authorized apps.

tokenRefreshableSeconds.label: Token refresh period
tokenRefreshableSeconds.help: Seconds. Sign in or authorize again after this period. Uses the validity period if it is longer.

tokensPerUser.label: Tokens per user
tokensPerUser.help: Tokens. Issuing a token removes the oldest launcher logins above this limit; each authorized app counts against its own limit.

loginIntervalMs.label: Login request interval
loginIntervalMs.help: Milliseconds. Sign-in and sign-out share an interval per username. 0 means no limit.

enabled.label: Maintenance mode
enabled.help: Everyone except admins and super admins sees the maintenance page, and the API returns 503. The sign-in page stays open so admins can sign in, do their work and turn this off.

blockProtocols.label: Also stop game services
blockProtocols.help: During maintenance, external login (Yggdrasil and Yggdrasil Connect) and CSL and USM skin loading also return 503: players cannot join servers that use this site for login, and skins do not show up in game. When unchecked, they keep working.

message.label: Maintenance message
message.help: Shown on the maintenance page. You can explain why and when you expect to be done. Leave it empty to show the default message.

trustedProxies.label: Trusted reverse proxies
trustedProxies.help: The client IP in X-Forwarded-For is only trusted for requests from these addresses. One IP or CIDR per line. A wrong value breaks the per-IP registration limit and rate limiting.

retentionDays.label: Audit log retention days
retentionDays.help: Audit logs older than this many days are automatically deleted each morning. Set to 0 to keep them forever.

publicMaxAge.label: Cache lifetime of public resources
publicMaxAge.help: How long browsers cache texture files and CSL responses, in seconds.

retentionDays.label: Notification retention days
retentionDays.help: Notifications are deleted this many days after they were sent, read or not. Set to 0 to keep them forever.

maxFileSizeMb.label: Log file size limit (MB)
maxFileSizeMb.help: When the log file being written in the logs/ folder of the data directory grows past this size, a new file is started. Takes effect within a minute after saving.

maxFiles.label: Log files to keep
maxFiles.help: How many log files to keep, including the one being written. Older files are deleted, so logs take up at most “size limit × files”. Takes effect within a minute after saving.

check.label: Check for updates
check.help: Read the release manifest from dl.nextskin.org once a day. No site information is sent.

themes.title: Themes
themes.description: The color themes users can choose from in their user center. Guests and users who haven't chosen one see the site default. Themes from plugins start out turned off: check that they suit your site before turning them on.
themes.defaultHint: The site default can't be turned off. Make another theme the default first.
themes.failed: Couldn't save. Please try again later.
themes.noPlugins: Only the built-in Diamond theme is available. Enable a plugin that provides themes (such as the official "More colors") and its themes will show up here.

invalid.title: Themes that failed the check
invalid.description: These themes have colors without enough contrast or that are too similar to tell apart, so they can't be turned on. Update the plugin once its author has fixed them.

themes.issue: In {mode, select, light {light} other {dark}} mode, {first} and {second} {check, select, contrast {have a contrast ratio of only {actual}, below {minimum}} distance {are only {actual} apart in OKLab, below {minimum}} other {have their lightness the wrong way round}} ({values})

missing.title: Themes currently unavailable
missing.description: These themes are turned on, but the plugin providing them is disabled or its new version no longer has them. Users who chose them see the site default for now, and get their choice back once the plugin does.

migration.title: Migration
migration.description: Import from Blessing Skin 6: the final sync before switching over, or importing old data into a site created with New site. Every run imports everything from the old database again and replaces this site's data.
migration.noticeTitle: The site is in maintenance while importing
migration.notice: Both dry runs and imports put the site in maintenance until they finish. Web imports only support single-instance deployments; for multiple instances, stop the service and use the node nextskin.mjs import blessing-skin command.
migration.empty: Dry runs and imports are listed here, each with its report.
migration.blocking: {count, plural, one {# blocking issue} other {# blocking issues}}
migration.newDescription: Do a dry run and read the report first, fix any blocking issues, then run the real import. Stop the old site for the last import: texture files aren't part of the database snapshot.

plugins.title: Plugins
plugins.description: Official plugins ship with the site; you can also upload third-party plugins, which run in a separate plugin host process. A plugin only runs once enabled. Installing, enabling, disabling and changing settings are all recorded in the audit log.
plugins.packageMissingHint: This instance can't get the package for the version in the plugins table (it isn't in storage, or it failed verification), so the plugin is unavailable here. If it intercepts registration, registration is paused. You can disable or uninstall it, or restore the package storage and wait a few seconds.
plugins.enableHint: Once enabled, the plugin runs on the server and can do everything listed under “What this plugin does”. Its tables are created first.
plugins.enableHighRisk: It uses high-risk capabilities: {list}. Only enable plugins you trust.
plugins.disableHint: Once disabled, the plugin stops handling events, registrations and requests, and anything it added to pages disappears. Its data, settings and queued jobs are kept and resume when you enable it again.
plugins.switchingHint: The plugin's status has changed; this instance switches over within a few seconds. Refresh the page to check.

deadLetters.title: Failed jobs
deadLetters.description: Jobs that still failed after several retries stop here and won't run again on their own. Once you've fixed the cause (a wrong setting, say), retry them. Shows the latest 50.
deadLetters.deleteHint: The job won't run again, and this can't be undone.

manifest.title: What this plugin does
manifest.formFields: Fields it adds to the sign-up form
manifest.fromQuery: Can be prefilled from a link

users.read: Read users' nicknames, roles and avatars
users.readPrivate: Read users' email addresses, score and language
users.score: Add to or deduct from any user’s score, and see balances

notifications.send: Send any user an in-site notification using the plugin’s own messages

storage.kv: Store a little data of its own

user.action: Manage players and textures: can refuse

providers.passwordHasher: Check passwords from an old system

host.failed: The plugin host kept crashing, so it is no longer restarted automatically. Uploaded plugins are paused: registrations that go through them are refused, and their jobs stay in the queue. Find the plugin causing it (you can disable it), then restart.
host.restarting: The plugin host is restarting. Uploaded plugins are unavailable for now.
host.networkUnrestricted: This server's Node.js can't stop uploaded plugins from connecting to the network directly, bypassing the site (Node.js 26 and later can). Requests a plugin makes through the site are still limited to the addresses it declares.

upload.label: Choose a plugin package
upload.trust: An uploaded plugin runs on the server and can do what is listed below. The site blocks data access beyond what it asks for, but it can't stop malicious code: this is a seat belt, not a sandbox. Plugins are not reviewed or signed, so only install plugins you trust.
upload.addedHint: The new version asks for the capabilities or external addresses marked “New” that {from} did not.
upload.upgradeEnabled: This plugin is running. Its tables are migrated and the new version is loaded first; the switch happens only if that works.
upload.upgradeDisabled: The plugin is not enabled and stays disabled after the upgrade.
upload.installHint: The plugin won't run until you enable it on its page.
upload.dropHint: The .tgz file made by nextskin-plugin build, up to 10 MiB.
upload.failed: Couldn't check this plugin package. Try again later.
upload.removedLogins: The new version removes these sign-in methods: {list}. Existing links are kept, but those users can’t sign in with them for now.

uninstall.title: Uninstall
uninstall.description: Uninstalling deletes the plugin's tables, stored data, settings, queued and failed jobs, and the uploaded package. This can't be undone. A running plugin is disabled first.
uninstall.dialogHint: The plugin's tables, stored data and settings will be deleted and can't be restored. To keep the data, disabling is enough.
uninstall.bindings: {bindings, plural, one {# linked account} other {# linked accounts}} from this plugin will also be deleted, and those users will have to link again. {stranded, plural, =0 {} one {# of them has no other way to sign in and will have to reset their password.} other {# of them have no other way to sign in and will have to reset their password.}}

logins.title: Third-party sign-in
logins.description: Paste the callback URL below into the app settings on the provider exactly as shown. If you change the site URL, the callback URL changes too and has to be updated on the provider.
logins.bindings: {count, plural, =0 {No linked accounts} one {# linked account} other {# linked accounts}}
logins.notHttps: The site URL is not HTTPS. The provider sends the authorization code to this site through the callback URL, and without encryption it can be intercepted; Google and Microsoft also reject non-HTTPS callback URLs. Change the site URL to HTTPS in Settings first.

score.title: Score
score.description: Score this plugin has added to or taken from users. Points a plugin gave out by mistake aren’t taken back automatically: disable the plugin first, then deduct them on each user’s detail page.
score.tableLabel: Recent score entries written by this plugin

updates.title: Updates
updates.description: Whether a new version is out, and how to upgrade this site. Checked once a day by reading a signed release list from dl.nextskin.org; nothing about the site is sent.
updates.upToDateHint: When a new stable release is out, it shows up here and in your notifications.
updates.unknownHint: Click “Check now”, or wait for the daily check.
updates.nodeTooOld: This version needs Node {required} or newer; the server runs {current}. Upgrade Node first.
updates.disabled: The release list is not read, and new versions are not announced.
updates.enable: Turn it on in advanced settings

failures.network: At {time}, dl.nextskin.org could not be reached. Check the network or proxy.
failures.invalid: At {time}, the release list was malformed or its signatures did not verify, so it was ignored.
failures.too_large: At {time}, the release list was too large, so it was ignored.

updates.failureHint: What you see below is from the last successful check.
updates.sourceTitle: Updates are not checked when running from source
updates.source: Pull the new code in the repository and rebuild. Use the release bundle or the image for production.

dockerSteps.backup: Back up the data volume first. SQLite is backed up into the data directory before migrations run; back up MySQL or PostgreSQL yourself.
dockerSteps.pull: Pull the new image and recreate the container:
dockerSteps.after: You cannot simply switch back to the old image afterwards: if there were migrations, the old version cannot open the migrated database, so restore the backup first.

bundleSteps.download: Download the new version's ZIP from GitHub Releases and verify it with SHA256SUMS on the same page.
bundleSteps.stop: Stop the service and back up. SQLite is backed up into the data directory before migrations run; back up MySQL or PostgreSQL yourself.
bundleSteps.unzip: Unzip over the current directory (.env and data/ stay as they are), then start as usual.

updates.privacy: Checking only reads one public file, and versions with bad signatures are dropped. To keep the site off the internet, turn checks off in advanced settings.
updates.oneClickManual: You can also upgrade by hand: download the ZIP, unzip it over the current directory and restart the service.
updates.managerUnreachable: One-click upgrades are unavailable for now. Restart the service; if that does not help, run node nextskin.mjs doctor on the server.

managerReasons.readonly: The manager process cannot write the program directory (releases/), so it only checks for updates. To upgrade with one click, see the “Upgrading” section for your deployment in the deployment guide.
managerReasons.unmanaged: The service was not started through the manager process (NEXTSKIN_MANAGER=off is set, or a version's launcher in releases/ was run directly), so upgrades are manual.

oneClick.ready: Prepare first: download, verify the signature, unzip, then check the new version against the database in use. The site keeps running; afterwards you see how long it will be down and whether to back up first.
oneClick.failedBefore: Last time this version failed its migrations here, or did not start after them. Preparing again downloads and checks it anew.
oneClick.stepping: {latest} needs a newer manager process than the one running now. Upgrade to {target} first, restart the service once so the manager it brings takes over, then come back and upgrade to {latest}.
oneClick.managerPending: The new manager process came with the last upgrade. Restart the service once to activate it, then you can upgrade to {version}.
oneClick.managerUnzip: One-click upgrade cannot reach this version, and there is no intermediate version to go through first. Upgrade by unzipping the {version} ZIP over the current directory, as described below.
oneClick.nothing: When a new stable release is out, upgrade it here with one click.

stepHints.preflight: Checking the new version against the database in use

oneClick.prepared: Download, verification and preflight passed. The site is still running {current}.
oneClick.migrationCount: {core, plural, other {# in core}}, {plugins, plural, one {# from an official plugin} other {# from official plugins}}
oneClick.downtimeValue: A few seconds to over thirty; the reverse proxy answers 502 meanwhile
oneClick.onFailure: If the new version does not come up

tiers.none: Switches back to the current version automatically; the database is untouched.
tiers.sqlite: The SQLite database is backed up before migrating; if the new version fails its health check, the backup and the current version are restored.
tiers.external-backup: If a migration fails, a PostgreSQL database is left as it was while a MySQL one may be left halfway; if the migrations succeed but the new version does not come up, nothing is rolled back. In each case restore from your own backup.

oneClick.incompatibleTitle: These plugins do not support the new version
oneClick.incompatible: The plugin API version each one requires is in parentheses. They will not load after the upgrade, so check the plugins page for new versions first.
oneClick.backup: This upgrade runs database migrations, and {dialect} cannot be rolled back automatically. Back it up the way you usually do (mysqldump, pg_dump, a snapshot of a managed database), then upgrade.
oneClick.applyDescription: The site will be down for a few seconds to over thirty; players cannot log in and textures do not load meanwhile.
oneClick.backupConfirm: I have backed up the {dialect} database
oneClick.switching: The site is down for a few seconds to over thirty, so it is normal that pages do not load meanwhile. This page refreshes itself once the new version is up.
oneClick.lostTitle: Still not back after five minutes
oneClick.lost: Check the service log on the server, or run node nextskin.mjs update status.
oneClick.lastFailedTitle: The upgrade to {to} did not succeed
oneClick.lastRolledBackTitle: The upgrade to {to} did not succeed; back on {from}
oneClick.lastRollbackFailedTitle: Going back to {to} did not succeed
oneClick.lastHint: {time}. Every result is recorded in releases/update-log.jsonl in the instance directory.

rollbackHints.plain: The last upgrade had no database migrations, so the {version} program is simply switched back in.
rollbackHints.sqlite: The SQLite database is replaced by the backup taken before the upgrade: every sign-up, upload and change since then is lost.
rollbackHints.external: With {dialect} migrations, rollback cannot be done from here: while the database is being restored, {current} would still be online and writing to it. Follow these steps on the server:

rollbackSteps.restore: Restore the {dialect} database from the backup taken before the upgrade.
rollbackSteps.command: Run the command below in the instance directory. It checks with {version} that the database really was restored, then switches back to {version} without starting the service.
rollbackSteps.start: Start the service. The site is back on {version}.

oneClick.rollbackBlocked: The SQLite backup taken before the upgrade is gone, so it cannot be rolled back automatically.

rollbackWarnings.plain: The site will be down for a few seconds to over thirty.
rollbackWarnings.sqlite: The database is replaced by the backup taken before the upgrade, and everything written since is lost. The site will be down for a few seconds to over thirty.

rollbackConfirms.sqlite: I understand everything written since the upgrade is lost

failedJobs.description: Core background jobs (sending email, deleting texture files, scheduled cleanups) that still failed after several tries stop here and will not run again on their own. Retry them once the cause is fixed. Only the last 30 days are kept.
failedJobs.pluginHint: Plugins' failed jobs are on each plugin's page.

names.textureSweep: Reclaim orphaned files in texture storage
names.auditLogCleanup: Clean up old audit log entries

errors.timeout: Timed out: the job ran longer than its limit
errors.error: Something went wrong; no details were recorded
errors.attempts_exhausted: The process exited in the middle of this job several times
errors.mail_not_configured: Email is not set up: the transport or sender address is empty

smtpCodes.EAUTH: Could not sign in to the SMTP server: wrong username or password
smtpCodes.ENOAUTH: The SMTP username or password is missing
smtpCodes.ECONNECTION: Couldn't connect to the SMTP server: wrong host, port or encryption, or the port is blocked
smtpCodes.ETIMEDOUT: The SMTP server did not respond
smtpCodes.EDNS: Couldn't resolve the SMTP server's address
smtpCodes.ETLS: TLS handshake failed: wrong encryption setting, or a problem with the server's certificate
smtpCodes.ESOCKET: The connection to the SMTP server dropped
smtpCodes.EPROTOCOL: The SMTP server sent an unexpected reply
smtpCodes.EENVELOPE: The server rejected the sender or recipient address
smtpCodes.EREQUIRETLS: The server doesn't support encrypted delivery

failedJobs.linkRemoved: The link in this email was removed, so it can't be retried. Ask the user to request it again.
failedJobs.notRetryable: Its content is incomplete, so it can't be retried.
failedJobs.noHandler: This version doesn't have this kind of job, so it can only be deleted.

failedJobs.deleteAllHint: Once deleted, these jobs won't run again and can't be restored. Jobs that failed after you opened this page aren't affected.

errors.user_not_found: This user could not be found. They may have deleted their account, or the account was deleted.
errors.user_banned: This user is banned and can't confirm a new email address. Unban them first, or use “Recover account” to change the email directly.
errors.last_login_method: This is the user's last working sign-in method. Set a password for them first, or use “Recover account”.
errors.external_account_not_found: This user doesn't have this linked account. It may already have been unlinked; refresh the page.
errors.email_unchanged: The new email is the same as the user's current email.
errors.email_taken: This email is already used by another account.
errors.texture_not_found: Texture not found, or it is a private texture the owner can't see.
errors.closet_item_exists: This texture is already in the user's closet.
errors.closet_item_not_found: This texture is not in the user's closet.

device.title: Authorize a launcher
device.enterDescription: Enter the code shown in your launcher or on your device to let it use your account.
device.invalid: That code wasn’t found, or it has already been used. Check the code in your launcher and enter it again.
device.expired: This code has expired. Go back to your launcher and sign in again.
device.claimed: This code was already opened by another account. Go back to your launcher and sign in again.
device.tooManyAttempts: Too many wrong codes. Try again in {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}.
device.warning: Only continue if you just started signing in on your own launcher or device. Never enter a code someone sent you.
device.approved: Go back to your launcher; it will finish signing in. You can close this page.
device.denied: {name} didn’t get any access. You can close this page.
